public_rationale: On July 30, 2024, Microsoft reported that AI services contributed eight percentage points to Azure revenue growth for the April–June 2024 quarter [e1, e2]. This was a reported contribution to realized quarterly growth, not an annualized revenue estimate [e1, e2]. Under the contract's reading that customer AI integrations include cloud AI services, Azure supplies a counterexample outside the exceptions for OpenAI's own revenue and AWS [e1]. The disclosure therefore contradicts the claimed absence of observable growth under that reading, while leaving the contribution from customer-built integrations alone unquantified [e1].
limitations: Microsoft's reported AI-services contribution does not separately quantify customer-built integrations; the assessment depends on the contract's broader reading [e1].
The growth attribution does not establish AI-services profitability [e1].
These disclosures do not verify the embedded OpenAI revenue and loss figures or the AWS revenue description; those exceptions are not separately assessed [e1, e2].

our_interpretation: The proposition being assessed is the absence of observable cloud-provider revenue growth from customer AI integrations, beyond the stated exceptions.
OpenAI's revenue and loss figures are embedded exceptions, not separate claims being graded here. No annualized figure is treated as realized annual revenue.
The ordinary reading includes revenue from cloud AI services through which organizations build applications and integrate models.
The OpenAI exception concerns OpenAI's own stated revenue; it does not exclude Microsoft's Azure AI services simply because some use OpenAI models.
The target is April–June 2024, the latest completed quarter publicly reportable before the post.
Microsoft Azure is an in-scope test of the general negative assertion. The metric scope records that counterexample and the company's reported attribution, without imposing a dollar threshold.
criteria.support_condition: Adequately comprehensive disclosures show no realized AI-services contribution to cloud revenue growth outside the stated exceptions during the target period.
criteria.contradiction_condition: An in-scope cloud provider publicly reports a positive realized revenue-growth contribution from AI services used for customer applications or integrations during the target period.
